description: Repairs r-cursor-1/seek-arguments: a fresh table-type recordset on PK_C already sits at (1,30), so every Seek that landed there could not be told from a Seek that did not move; the recovery step Seek =,1,30 had the same weakness. Table C holds (1,10),(1,20),(1,30),(2,10); Index PK_C is A ASC, B DESC. For each of two start positions [the last row (MoveLast); the third row (MoveFirst, Move 2)] and each argument list of Seek [= 1, 20; = 1; = (no key); = Missing, 20; = 1, Null; = Null, Null; = Empty, Empty; = "1", "20"; = "abc", 20; = 1.5, 20; = 1, 20, 5; >= 1; > 1; <= 1; < 2; == 1, 20]: a fresh table-type recordset over C, Index PK_C, moved to the start position; read A and B (the start); Seek with the arguments; read Errors; read NoMatch, BOF, EOF, A and B; MoveNext and read A and B; close. Then, from each start, on one fresh recordset: Seek "=", 9, 9 and read Errors, NoMatch, BOF, EOF, A and B; Seek "=", 1, 30 and read NoMatch, A and B; MovePrevious and read A and B. The two starts are different rows, so a landing row that equals one start is told from a Seek that did not move by the other run. Asks the omission, Null, coercion and wrong-type policy of Seek and the recovery after a failed Seek. The fixture copy is opened read-only.
